subject: Request: temporary adjustment to P1/P2 response windows for EU peak hours
messages:
From: Anna Ross <anna.ross@clearpay.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary adjustment to P1/P2 response windows for EU peak hours

Hi Mina,

We're seeing a repeated spike in latency for our EU region between 02:00-06:00 UTC tied to batch jobs that increase peak token throughput. It's causing a handful of P2 incidents to tip into P1 by our monitoring. Our ops team would like to request a temporary change to the support response windows so the on-call rotation aligns with the new load pattern while we optimize batching.

Specifically: can Redwood grant a 30-day, time-boxed exception to the current P1 30-min response SLA for the hours 02:00-06:00 UTC, moving to a 45-min P1 window during that window, and extend P2 to 3 hours? We understand this is material — we want to document reasons and an explicit rollback date.

We're happy to share telemetry and have a short call to walk through the telemetry and mitigation plan. Please let me know the process and any forms needed.

Thanks,
Anna Ross
Head of Platform Ops | ClearPay
anna.ross@clearpay.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Anna Ross <anna.ross@clearpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary adjustment to P1/P2 response windows for EU peak hours

Hi Anna — thanks for the heads up and for the concrete windows. We're open to a structured, time-boxed exception when there's a clear mitigation plan and rollback.

Next steps from our side:
- Please complete the attached SLO exception form (slo_exception_form.pdf) with the telemetry links and expected rollback date.
- Ben (Sales Ops) will confirm commercial/contract implications for SLA amendments.
- Rishi (Support Operations) will propose an on-call rotation tweak and escalation path during the exception window.

Tentative timeline: if you can return the form by EOD 2028-08-03, we can stand up a short approval thread and aim to implement the change by 2028-08-07 (subject to approval).

I'll also schedule a 30-minute working session with the three of us to review the telemetry.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com

Attachment: slo_exception_form.pdf (form stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Anna Ross <anna.ross@clearpay.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-03T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary adjustment to P1/P2 response windows for EU peak hours

Thanks Anna — received the filled form and telemetry link (thanks for the quick turnaround). Quick commercial notes:
- A formal SLO amendment for a 30-day time-boxed waiver requires sign-off from account execs and legal. For short waivers we can process it as an "operational SLA exception" that doesn't change billing, but it must be logged and approved.
- If ClearPay wants a higher-fidelity guarantee during peak hours (e.g., dedicated capacity), we can draft options but that's separate.

For now, Mina — can you and Rishi confirm the on-call changes that would be implemented operationally so we can include them in the exception doc? Rishi, suggested approach below:
- Add a temporary EU-focused on-call slot covering 01:30-06:30 UTC for the duration of the exception
- Primary responder: rotation drawn from EU M-F roster; fallback: global P1 responder with 45-min window
- Escalation path: first escalate to Support Lead (Rishi), then to CS Director (Mina), then to Sales/Account Exec if not acknowledged in 90 minutes

I'll open the operational ticket and attach the signed form once we have those details.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachment: oncall_rotation_sheet.csv (proposed shift times)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Anna Ross <anna.ross@clearpay.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-05T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary adjustment to P1/P2 response windows for EU peak hours

Anna — we've reviewed the telemetry with the infra team this morning. We can implement the exception with the following guardrails: 

Operational plan (summary):
- Effective window: 2028-08-07 00:00 UTC through 2028-09-06 23:59 UTC (30 days).
- SLA during window: P1 = 45-minute initial response, P2 = 3-hour initial response for incidents detected between 02:00-06:00 UTC. Outside those hours, standard SLAs remain in force.
- On-call changes: temporary EU-focused cover 01:30-06:30 UTC; rotation pulled from existing EU responders (see attached CSV). Global fallback responder retains standard escalation rights.
- Escalation path: primary on-call -> Support Lead (Rishi) within 45 minutes -> CS Director (Mina) within 90 minutes -> Account Exec (Ben) within 3 hours for commercial impact.
- Telemetry & rollback criteria: if token latency or error rate does not improve by 20% within 14 days, we'll trigger a mitigation review and either accelerate batching fixes or revert SLA to standard.

Compliance & documentation: we'll log the exception in the operations registry and attach the filled SLO exception form and rotation CSV. Ben will route approvals through legal for an "operational SLA exception" note.

Anna, please confirm acceptance of the window and sign-off on the rollback criteria. If we get your sign-off, Ben will attach the documents and we'll activate the change on 2028-08-07 as planned.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Support Operations Lead | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
